To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

young, urban, African-American and Latina women engage in unprotected sex with men they distrust and perceive to be at high risk for HIV infection because of their desire to maintain hope, a sense of sensuality, and a sense of intimacy and stability in their relationship.

young urban women’s patterns of unprotected sex with men engaging in HIV risk behaviors can be understood by examining the power dynamics between men and women and how these dynamics are played out in the context of sexual encounters.
the women in our study reported that they engaged in unprotected sex because they were in love with their partners and they wanted their partners to be satisfied.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding how low power sex scripts can be transformed to high power sex scripts and how this transformation may reduce the risk of HIV.
the ways that women’s power is used to protect themselves from HIV infection and how they are affected by their own and others’ powerlessness in relation to HIV risk.
the development of an intervention that will empower urban women to reduce the risk of HIV transmission by increasing their awareness of the salient risks and their power to act on that knowledge.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the patterns of unprotected sex are a result of the women’s low sense of self-worth, low self-esteem and low self-respect, and the lack of self-awareness of the women’s needs and desires, and the lack to know their own value.
the patterns of unprotected sex with men perceived to engage in high HIV risk behaviors were influenced by the power women felt in their relationship and the sex scripts they were socialized to use.

the patterns of unprotected sex with men engaging in HIV risk behaviors are the result of a combination of factors including the women’s low self esteem, their desire to please their partners, and their lack of awareness of their own value.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the patterns of unprotected sex that women engage in with male partners they distrust and perceive to engage in HIV risks are a result of the powerlessness that they experience in the context of their relationship with these men.
young urban women’s patterns of unprotected sex with men engaging in HIV risk behaviors is a usual practice for them.
women’s power is an essential component in the prevention and treatment of HIV/AIDS and other sexually transmitted infections.
The main takeaway from our work is that
women are not passive in their sexual encounters.
women’s sexual agency can be enhanced by increasing awareness of their own power and by increasing awareness of the salience of HIV risk.
women are capable of change and can be powerful in their relationships with men.
